thread:
Nina: saw a persistent parse flake on kestrel-v2q int8 canary: structured funcalls sometimes arrive with keys reordered or a trailing optional field missing, failing strict validators. @Omar @Sasha

Nina: small repro:
```
{"meta":{"id":"a1"},"action":"create_ticket","body":{"summary":"x"}}
# vs sometimes
{"action":"create_ticket","body":{"summary":"x"}}
```

Omar: how often?

Nina: ~0.7% strict_parse_fail over 2k requests; soft-retry recovers ~60%. failures spike at batch sizes 1-3 and prompts <40 tokens.

Felix: likely two causes: nondeterministic output order + tokenization truncation dropping trailing keys.

Sasha: quick mitigation: opt-in route-level "canonicalize_on_parse" shim that normalizes key order to schema, inserts missing optional keys as null, then runs strict validation. telemetry: canonicalizer_invocations and rewrites.

Omar: add telemetry to tag reason: order_mismatch, missing_key, nonjson so we can prioritize.

Nina: added 2% trace sampling to s3 for diffs: https://redwood-internal/s3/canaries/1745009999/traces

CanaryBot: run summary kestrel-v2q-int8 2024-04-02T09:12:00Z requests=2048 strict_parse_fail=0.7% retries=12 avg_latency_ms=39

Felix: next plan: 1) implement shim (Sasha) 2) add schema-shuffle and truncation cases to fuzz-suite (Nina) 3) split parse-failure telemetry (Omar) 4) small PTQ tweak experiment for very short prompts (<32 tokens)

Sasha: will prototype shim with route flag {"toolrouter":{"canonicalize_on_parse":true}} and sampled diffs. preserve_order flag for legacy handlers.

Nina: I'll run a targeted canary with shim toggled and report back in onboarding sync. :thumbsup:
